title: Chapter 7 — The War Chest
description: Campaigns eat money. Donors want favours, Baba Oko wants a contract, Funke finds an envelope, and Owó Ńlá sends his boys.

beats.speaker: seyi
beats.text: Teacher, we are finished. (He shows you the books, a school exercise book with a cartoon on the cover.) Posters, agents, diesel, Mama Titi's "association", the boys who guard the posters at night. We need ₦120,000 by next week or the campaign dies of hunger.

beats.speaker: seyi
beats.text: Where does the money come from?

options.text: "We hold a fundraiser on Rich Street. We sell... access."
"We raise it ourselves. Rallies, dance-offs, small donations. Slow and clean."

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Rich Street. A garden with fairy lights and a man whose only job is to refill the Chapman. The donors don't give money. They buy promises: a road contract, a permit, a "consideration".

beats.speaker: seyi
beats.text: Name your price for each promise. Too cheap and you look desperate. Too expensive and they go to Owó Ńlá. He is having a sale.

beats.speaker: seyi
beats.text: Clean money is slow money, Teacher. ₦120,000. Rallies at the Front Stop, the owambe dance-offs, anything honest. Tell me when the box is full.

beats.objective: Raise ₦120,000 for the campaign the clean way (rallies, dance-offs, small jobs). Then go back to Seyi at the office.

beats.speaker: seyi
beats.text: (He counts it twice.) Two hundred small donations. A pepper seller gave ₦200 and made me write her name down. ...Okay. Maybe clean money has a better smell.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A text from an unknown number: "Baba says come." The Prado is already outside.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Baba Oko does not take no the first time. Or the second.

beats.speaker: babaOko
beats.text: Teacher. The market toilet contract, the one you are promising everybody. When you win, my nephew Wale will build it. ₦40 million. He has a company. It has a name and everything.

beats.speaker: babaOko
beats.text: Sign here. It is just a letter of intention.

options.text: "After I win, we will open a tender. Wale can bid like everybody."
Fold the letter and put it in your pocket. "Let me read it at home."

beats.speaker: babaOko
beats.text: (He watches you like a man watching a goat he has already paid for.) Good. Go well.

variants.text: (He smiles with his teeth only.) A tender. In Iyana-Wahala. You are a funny man, Teacher. Funny men are very good at funerals.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Funke is standing at the kitchen table. On the table is a brown envelope. On the envelope, in Seyi's handwriting: "Donor 4: the road permit".

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Funke is standing at the kitchen table. On the table is a folded letter on Baba Oko's letterhead. She found it in your trouser pocket, doing the washing.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Funke is standing at the kitchen table with your phone. Seyi texted at 2 a.m.: "Baba Oko is not happy. Call him before he calls other people."

beats.speaker: funke
beats.text: Explain it to me like I am one of your JSS 2 students.

beats.speaker: funke
beats.text: She has not raised her voice. That is the frightening part.

options.text: Tell her the truth. All of it.
"I needed it. Everybody does it. You don't understand this world."

beats.speaker: funke
beats.text: Okay.

variants.text: (Long pause.) I told you. I would know before you finished the sentence. (She goes to bed. You hear her lock the door, gently.)
(She sits down.) Thank you for not lying. Now I am frightened and angry at the same time, and you will have to sleep beside both.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Midnight. Glass breaks at the campaign office. Four boys in Owó Ńlá's colours are tearing down the posters, and one of them has the generator on his shoulder like a baby.

beats.speaker: seyi
beats.text: (On the phone, out of breath.) Teacher! They are carrying the generator! Come with your whole body!

won.toast: The boys run. Somebody filmed it. You look like a man who fights for his ward.

beats.speaker: seyi
beats.text: They took the generator.

variants.text: Teacher! (He is laughing and shaking.) You beat Owó Ńlá's boys with a campaign poster. This video will sell more than rice.

beats.title: The War Chest
beats.summary: You found the money, one way or another. Everybody who gave it is keeping a receipt in their head.
